newsitem.title: BULGARIA: BULGARIA HOPES TO COMPLETE SOLVAY DEAL BY FEB 28.
newsitem.headline: BULGARIA HOPES TO COMPLETE SOLVAY DEAL BY FEB 28.

text.p: Bulgaria is expected to finalise the sell-off of 60 percent of major soda ash producer Sodi-Devnya to Belgian chemical group Solvay SA by the end of the month, a government spokeswoman said.
"Prime minister Stefan Sofianski and Solvay representatives outlined details for finalisation of the deal by February 28," the spokeswoman told reporters, declining to elaborate.
Solvay said in December it had signed a preliminary agreement with Bulgaria's Privatisation Agency allowing it to acquire 60 percent of Sodi for $160 million.

The deal, signed with the former Socialist government did not include ownership of adjacent lime and salt quarries and a nearby thermal power plant supplying Sodi. Solvay representatives asked for clear conditions of their use, said the spokeswoman.
The interim cabinet headed by Sofianski took office on Thursday and will rule until the new parliament is elected on April 19.
Bulgaria relies on the proceeds from the deal to service its foreign debt payments.
The proceeds should be transferred to the State Fund for Reconstruction and Development, from which Bulgaria used $135 million for the Brady bond coupon payments last month.
So far Solvay has transferred to Bulgaria a total of $60 million under the deal.
